headline: GOLD DETHRONES US TREASURIES: ECB Confirms 27% Reserve Share as Central Banks Hoard 36,000 Tonnes
snippet: The European Central Bank confirmed gold has displaced US Treasuries as the world's second-largest reserve asset, with bullion now at 27% of global central bank portfolios versus 22% for Treasuries — up from 20% vs. 25% a year ago. Sustained buying by China, Poland, Turkey and India has reshaped reserve portfolios, with total central bank gold holdings approaching 36,000 tonnes, levels last seen under the Bretton Woods system.

headline: DISCOVERY SILVER CLOSES Glencore's Kidd Creek: Copper-Zinc-Silver Mine Adds 10–15K Tonnes Zinc in 2026
snippet: Discovery Silver Corp. completed its acquisition of Glencore's 100% interest in the Kidd Operations in Timmins, Ontario on June 1, including the Kidd Creek copper-zinc-silver mine and metallurgical complex. Expected 2026 production from the acquired assets includes 10–15K tonnes of zinc, 5–7K tonnes of copper, and ~400K oz of silver, with the deal providing infrastructure to support doubling annual gold production across the broader Timmins camp.

headline: NORTHERN STAR SURGES 12.4% After High-Grade Gold Drill Intercepts at Pogo Mine, Alaska
snippet: Northern Star Resources (ASX:NST) led the ASX 200 with a 12.4% gain to a new 52-week high on June 2 after reporting high-grade gold intercepts from drilling at its Pogo mine in Alaska and key Western Australian operations. Analysts noted the results exceeded expectations and reinforced FY2026 production guidance, with the stock now offering clear leverage to $4,500+ gold.

headline: GOLD WHIPSAWS Near $4,490 as Iran Talks Stall and Fed Rate-Hike Probability Climbs to 68%
snippet: Gold oscillated between $4,490 and $4,546 on June 2 as US-Iran ceasefire negotiations stalled, stoking oil-driven inflation concerns and lifting market pricing for a Federal Reserve rate hike before year-end to 68%. The metal recovered briefly from June 1 lows on a dip in oil prices but remains hostage to Middle East developments with no deal in sight.

headline: GHANA GOES TO 30%: Central Bank Begins Buying 30% of Large Miners' Output to Build 157-Tonne Reserve
snippet: Ghana's central bank increased its mandatory gold purchase requirement from large-scale producers to 30% of output from 20%, effective June 1, with a target of building 157 tonnes in reserves by 2028. The policy switches from refined gold to doré for domestic processing, though Ghana Chamber of Mines CEO Kenneth Ashigbey says pricing and discount negotiations remain 'not straightforward.'

headline: NEW FOUND GOLD Deploys Six Rigs on $44M Queensway Push — 90,000 Metres Planned, 32,000 Already Down
snippet: New Found Gold Corp. (TSX:NFGC) expanded its Queensway Gold Project in Newfoundland to six active drill rigs under a fully funded $44M program targeting 90,000 metres in 2026, with 32,000 metres already completed. Initial holes focus on resource conversion in the Appleton Fault Zone Core while new exploration rigs fan out across the 220,000-hectare land package seeking additional discovery.

headline: SILVER STUMBLES Below $75 After $89 May Peak — Record 215Moz Deficit Enters Sixth Consecutive Year
snippet: Silver reversed below $75 per ounce in early June after hitting a two-month high of $89.4 in mid-May, pressured by stalled Middle East peace talks, hawkish Fed expectations, and investor position unwinding. The Silver Institute projects a record 215 million ounce deficit for 2026 — the sixth consecutive year of shortfall — with cumulative drawdowns from above-ground stocks reaching 762 million ounces since 2021.

headline: COPPER HITS $6.56 as J.P. Morgan Flags 330,000-Tonne Deficit — AI, Electrification and Defence Demand Surge
snippet: Copper climbed to $6.56 per pound on June 2 — up 35.7% year-over-year — as J.P. Morgan projected a 330,000-tonne refined copper deficit in 2026 driven by mine supply disruptions and surging demand from AI data centers, power grid electrification, and defence spending. Chile's April copper output hit a 23-year low, and the Grasberg Block Cave closure in Indonesia has added further strain to an already tight supply picture.

headline: MAGNUM MINING Jumps 9% on Azimuth Rare Earth Project Progress in Brazil — Drill Results Imminent
snippet: Magnum Mining and Exploration (ASX:MGU) shares surged 9.09% on June 1 after releasing an operational update on its Azimuth Rare Earth Elements project in Brazil, outlining expanded drill coverage and advancement toward key exploration milestones. The move underscores growing investor appetite for non-China rare earth development as Beijing's 2025 export controls continue to rattle Western supply chains.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $85 as Denison Phoenix Breaks Ground — First New Permitted Canadian Uranium Mine in a Decade
snippet: Uranium spot prices held near $85 per pound as Denison Mines' Phoenix in-situ recovery project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin became the first fully permitted uranium mine to enter construction in over a decade. Utilities remain structurally under-contracted — with only 116 million pounds secured against a 150 million pound replacement need — building toward a significant demand wave into the 2030s.

headline: GOLDEN GYRATION: Gold and Silver Whipsaw as Irksome Inflation Reasserts Itself — What the Charts Say
snippet: With gold and silver both failing to hold top-three positions in the year-to-date BEGOS Markets rankings — while oil, copper and the S&P 500 lead — a GoldSeek analyst argues the metals complex is consolidating before the next leg higher, not rolling over. Gold has traded in a narrow 5% range while silver swung 12%, setting up what the author sees as a decisive range resolution tied to the inflation and Fed rate trajectory.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE SURGE Rescues Lithium Demand Outlook — Battery Storage to Hit 31% of Consumption in 2026
snippet: A surge in battery energy storage installations — driven by China's power sector reforms — is transforming the demand outlook for lithium after years of painful oversupply. Broker Guotai Junan projects lithium carbonate demand from energy storage will account for 31% of overall consumption in 2026, up from 23% in 2025, with Chile's lithium export revenue already hitting US$2.1 billion in the first four months of the year.
